new_entities.name: Colonoscopy screening age 50 to 75
new_entities.description: Screening colonoscopy performed in adults aged 50 to 75 years.

edges.effect_quant: Randomized and instrumental-variable analyses now support lower colorectal cancer mortality with colonoscopy screening, while broader meta-analyses across screening modalities consistently place colonoscopy on the protective side for colorectal death reduction.
edges.population: average-risk adults in the usual screening age range of about 50 to 75 years
edges.mechanism: Colonoscopy reduces colorectal cancer mortality both by detecting cancers at earlier, more curable stages and by removing premalignant adenomas before invasive cancer develops.
edges.summary: This is one of the sturdier screening edges in the corpus. Even though effect sizes differ across intention-to-screen, per-protocol, and observational frameworks, the directional signal that colonoscopy lowers colorectal cancer mortality is consistent enough to classify as protective.
edges.caveats: Absolute benefit depends on participation, bowel preparation quality, adenoma detection quality, and competing mortality. The balance of benefit versus procedural harm is not represented in this mortality-only edge.
